simple_description: Extremely brief, sharp, needle-like or ice-pick stabbing pains in the head that last only a few seconds, occurring unpredictably in one or multiple spots without nausea or autonomic symptoms.
medical_description: Transient, sharp, lancinating jabs of head pain that occur spontaneously, lasting typically from a fraction of a second up to a few seconds, localized to the distribution of the first division of the trigeminal nerve (ophthalmic branch V1) or parietal/temporal scalp, with no autonomic symptoms and normal neuroimaging. Highly responsive to indomethacin.
affected_system: Trigeminal nerve sensory root (V1 division), epicranial nerve endings, and thalamocortical sensory pathways.
symptoms: Sudden, ultra-sharp, stabbing pain like a needle, nail, or ice-pick poking into the skull
Duration strictly very brief (typically 1 to 3 seconds, rarely up to 10 seconds)
Single jab or irregular volleys of stabs occurring throughout the day
Can occur in a single spot or wander to different regions of the scalp
Absence of autonomic signs (no tearing, no runny nose, no redness in eyes)
Absence of nausea, vomiting, photophobia, or phonophobia
early_warning_signs: None; stabs strike completely spontaneously without warning or prodrome
possible_causes: Focal episodic hyper-excitability of epicranial terminal sensory nerve branches (trigeminal and occipital nerve endings)
risk_factors: Co-existing history of migraine or cluster headache (stabbing headache is common in migraineurs)
disease_types: Fixed-site primary stabbing headache (requiring structural imaging to rule out local pathology)
clinical_evaluation: Clinical diagnosis according to ICHD-3 criteria 4.7. Complete neurological examination is completely normal. Palpation of scalp may occasionally reveal localized cutaneous tenderness.
diagnostic_tests: 3T Brain MRI with cranial nerve protocol - Required if stabs occur strictly in a single fixed location to rule out structural intracranial lesion, meningioma, or vascular malformation
treatment_overview: Reassurance is the cornerstone because individual stabs last only seconds. If frequent or debilitating, Indomethacin is the gold-standard therapeutic agent.
medication_classes: Indomethacin (NSAID) - Distinctively effective diagnostic and therapeutic agent
Melatonin (3 to 12 mg at bedtime) - Well-tolerated non-NSAID alternative
Gabapentin or Celecoxib for refractory cases
precautions: Do not confuse with trigeminal neuralgia (which affects V2/V3 lower face and is triggered by chewing/touching)
Do not confuse with migraine (which is pulsating and lasts hours with nausea)
prevention: Indomethacin prophylaxis when attack frequency is high
complications: High anxiety and fear of serious brain disease due to the startling sharpness of the pain
emergency_signs: Pain that becomes continuous rather than lasting seconds
Accompanied by facial numbness, double vision, or limb weakness
Associated with high fever or altered consciousness

faqs.question: Is an ice-pick headache a sign of a brain tumor?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Primary stabbing headache is a benign primary disorder. However, if the stabbing occurs strictly in one single fixed point repeatedly, a neurologist will order an MRI to rule out any underlying structural cause.

faqs.question: How is it different from Migraine?
faqs.answer: Ice-pick pain lasts only 1 to 3 seconds like a sudden needle poke. Migraine lasts 4 to 72 hours, is throbbing, and is accompanied by nausea and light sensitivity.

hi.name: प्राइमरी स्टैबिंग सिरदर्द (Ice-Pick Headache)
hi.summary: सिर में अचानक सुई या कील चुभने जैसा बहुत तेज़ दर्द जो सिर्फ 1 से 3 सेकंड रहता है और फिर गायब हो जाता है।
hi.advice: घबराएं नहीं, यह दर्द कुछ सेकंड में शांत हो जाता है। यदि यह दिन में बार-बार हो तो न्यूरोलॉजिस्ट से इंडोमेथासिन दवा के लिए परामर्श लें।

hinglish.name: Ice-Pick Headache (Sui chubhan jaisa tez dard)
hinglish.summary: Sir me achanak sui jaisa teekha jhatka lagna jo sirf 1-3 seconds rehta hai aur bina ulti ke hota hai.
hinglish.advice: Ghabrayein nahi, yeh migraine nahi hai. Local ice pack lagayein aur neurologist se milen.

ur.name: پرائمری سٹیبنگ سر درد (سوئی جیسی چبھن)
ur.summary: سر میں اچانک سوئی چبھنے جیسا شدید درد جو صرف چند سیکنڈ رہتا ہے اور خود بخود ختم ہو جاتا ہے۔
ur.advice: یہ عام طور پر خطرناک نہیں ہوتا، پرسکون رہیں اور ڈاکٹر سے رجوع کریں۔
